draft.title: Discursive writing
card: A discursive text explores an idea from several angles. Its aim is to think about the idea, not to win an argument.
It is reflective and often personal. The writer may draw on their own memories, doubts and observations as they think.
It can weigh up views that pull in different directions, and the writer may admit they are unsure.
It can end on a question or an open thought rather than a firm conclusion. A persuasive text, by contrast, pushes the reader towards one view.
draft.remember: Discursive writing explores an idea and may stay open. Persuasive writing pushes one view.

a.q: Which description best fits a discursive text?
opts: It explores an idea from several angles and may stay open
It argues for one view and dismisses all the others
It tells a story through characters, setting and plot
It presents facts in a neutral and impersonal tone
a.why: A discursive text thinks through an idea and need not reach a final answer. A text that argues one view is persuasive, which is the most tempting wrong option, because a discursive writer is not trying to win.
a.clue: Think about whether the writer is trying to win or to explore.

b.q: Priya writes about her grandmother's garden. She recalls it fondly, wonders if growing things slows life down, considers that it may just be nostalgia, and ends by asking what she really misses. What type of writing is this?
opts: Discursive, as it weighs an idea and ends on a question
Persuasive, as it uses personal memories to prove a point
Informative, as it explains how gardens affect people
Imaginative, as it describes a garden in vivid detail
b.why: Priya looks at the idea from more than one angle, admits doubt and ends on a question, which are signs of discursive writing. Her personal memories do not make it persuasive, because she is not trying to win the reader to one view.
b.clue: Does Priya reach a firm conclusion, or leave the idea open?

a.best: It explores an idea from several angles and may stay open

b.best: Discursive, as it weighs an idea and ends on a question
